description: The source has an anomalous word before 'of the punishment'; translation marks the contextually probable sense 'cessation' as supplied.
Greek 'Manifestation and Truth' is retained as a title-like pair in the high-priestly cultic context.
The compact comparison 'like the filling of a threshing floor' has uncertain precise force; both versions preserve the agricultural image.
Source contains a Latin intrusion, compressed uncertain syntax, and a lacuna inside the identifiable Genesis 49:27 quotation; restoration is disclosed in the translation note.
A short transmitted clause is corrupt or elliptical and the final contrast is compressed; both versions disclose the uncertainty.
Defective words occur after the reference to Mary bearing the Savior; the translation retains only the secure surrounding argument.
The legal commentary is severely elliptical and contains a visible text break; supplied syntax is marked and the readable version declines to reconstruct the full sequence.
The list of manna translation variants ends in syntactically insecure expressions; literal remnants are preserved without speculative explanation.
JSONL locus and printed verse number disagree, and a short Greek phrase is semantically uncertain.
The surviving one-sentence comment is irrecoverably elliptical; translation states only the secure references to seer, fee, and bringing him.
The final Greek noun is anomalously feminine 'ladies/mistresses'; it is disclosed rather than silently normalized.
Several obvious spelling defects affect the words for vowed, Jephthah, and Lord; secure contextual senses are translated and the defects disclosed.
The catena preserves several unusual transliterated test-words in its account of the dialect password; no unsupported linguistic identification is added.
The explanation that barrenness is from present ministry rather than nature is semantically compressed.
A compressed clause connects the Hebrew word's extension or application with the synagogue; contextual sense is bracketed and noted.
Several defective word forms occur in the long gate interpretation; secure syntax is translated and the forms are listed in textual notes.
CGPG record contains repeated spelling, spacing, and inflectional damage; probable readings are marked, including the likely adjective 'very young'.
Several phrases remain damaged or ambiguous, especially the wording concerning naming prophets; both versions avoid a definite reconstruction.
Hostile religious polemic with historically unreliable and defamatory assertions; framing is retained so claims are not mistaken for project endorsement.
The transmitted bird list and several explanatory clauses contain malformed or compressed readings; both versions preserve only defensible senses and disclose the damage.
The selected record begins in the middle of a sentence, so both translations explicitly mark its fragmentary opening.
The long spiritual interpretation contains numerous OCR or transmission defects; contextual supplements and unresolved wording are disclosed rather than presented as secure text.
The JSONL locus is 24.12 while the preserved printed verse heading is Deuteronomy 24:6; the translation retains and explains the disagreement.
